title: Restriction to an invariant scheme-theoretic image
statement: For a projective finite-type k-scheme Z with an ample PGL-linearized invertible module L, a quasi-compact invariant map j:J→Z, and a closed immersion i:X→Z with the same kernel ideal as j, there is a restricted linearized action E on i*L. A geometric point of X is E-semistable exactly when its image in Z is semistable. The field, action, ample module and image have the meanings in [def-weil-field], [def-sfb-pgl-linearized-polarization], [def-sc-ample] and [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure].

source.place: MFK GIT Chapter 1 Theorem 1.10 and Appendix 1.C; Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3 Sections 8–9. The source-specific proof is written in the Lean docstring. Section-ring action uses Stacks 02KH; section finiteness uses Stacks 0B5T. Local MFK book is WANTED.

proof.text: Restrict the scheme action to the scheme-theoretic image by flat schematic density of GL times J in GL times X. Restrict the line isomorphisms using pullback composition; cancellation and pullback coherence transfer all identities.

Use eventual surjectivity of restriction of polarized sections and homogeneous invariant power lifting on symmetric algebras. Restriction gives one semistability implication, and an invariant lift of a positive power gives the reverse.

lean.statement:
theorem invariant_image_restriction
    (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (hprojective : IsHProjective Z.hom)
    (hfiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType Z.hom ∧ QuasiCompact Z.hom)
    (L : Z.left.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (hample : IsAmple Z.hom L)
    (D : Action k r Z L) (J : Over (Spec (.of k))) (j : J ⟶ Z)
    (hqc : QuasiCompact j.left) (hinvariant : D.IsInvariantSubscheme j)
    (X : Over (Spec (.of k))) (i : X ⟶ Z) (hclosed : IsClosedImmersion i.left)
    (himage : i.left.ker = j.left.ker) :
    ∃ E : Action k r X ((Scheme.Modules.pullback i.left).obj L),
      D.IsRestriction i E ∧
      ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra k Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
        (x : fieldTest k Ω ⟶ X),
        E.IsSemistable Ω x ↔ D.IsSemistable Ω (x ≫ i)
